subject: English
passage:
While researching a topic, a student has taken the following notes:
• Wetlands develop when water accumulates in an area with poor drainage over extended periods.
• A wetland experiencing rapid plant growth and high biodiversity is called a thriving wetland.
• Eutrophication is a process in which a wetland becomes overloaded with nutrients.
• A wetland that can no longer support diverse plant and animal life is called a degraded wetland.
• A degraded wetland has entered the collapse phase.
prompt: The student wants to explain what a degraded wetland is. Which choice most effectively uses relevant information from the notes to accomplish this goal?

choices.A: Before eutrophication, a thriving wetland will support plant growth and high biodiversity.
choices.B: Having entered the collapse phase, a degraded wetland is one that can no longer support diverse plant and animal life.
choices.C: When it becomes degraded, a thriving wetland enters the collapse phase.
choices.D: A thriving wetland will become overloaded with nutrients and eventually become degraded.

explanation:
Choice B is the best answer. This choice defines a degraded wetland as "one that can no longer support diverse plant and animal life."

Why D is incorrect:

Choice D is incorrect. This choice only describes what causes degradation.
